amanda: quick heads-up — on the magnet-16b-int4 bring-up i ran a short smoke across long-context (seq 8k) and saw token divergence when the kvcache rolls over. not a full repro but consistent drift when we cross a ~4k boundary.

devon: hmm, drift how? model outputs different logits or generation stops?

amanda: logits diverge, generation continues. looks like certain attention keys get reused incorrectly after the wrap. i dumped a small kvcache fingerprint, attaching snippet below.

amanda: ```
KV-FP: shard0:0x7fa12a3b shard1:0x3b9f2c1e shard2:0x00000000 shard3:0x9cabf211
step 4095 -> ok
step 4096 -> shard2 becomes zeroed then reused
seq=4096->8192 transition shows repeated keys
```

sanjay: could be index arithmetic when we convert rotary positions -> cache slot. did you run with rotary scaling enabled?

amanda: rotary scaling=true. turning it off made the oddity less frequent but not gone. suspect two issues: 1) ring index wrap handling in the cache allocator, 2) quantized memcpy padding clearing extra bytes.

lia: do we have a minimal repro script? even a short prompt that reliably flips after N tokens would help.

amanda: i have a short repro; steps: 1) seed with 2k tokens prime, 2) stream 6k tokens of repeating pattern A->B, 3) check logits at token 4096 and 4097. i'll drop it in the repo later.

ben: thanks. can you dump the raw kvtile indices around the boundary? i want to verify whether slot idx = (pos & mask) or pos % window. also include dtype alignments (int4 pack offsets).

amanda: will do, quick dump shows masking is used but mask value maybe wrong for our tiled layout: mask=0xfff (4095) while tile_stride=4096. looks suspicious.

ci-bot: automated test run queued: ml-smoke/window-resilience/1750001234. expect logs in ~12m. :gear:

devon: if mask==4095 and stride==4096 then pos & mask should be ok up to 4095; when pos==4096 we want new slot but if some code uses >> instead of &, could cause stale pointer. good catch.

lia: also check memcpy paths in quantized kernel. int4 pack sometimes uses memset to clear tail bytes; if tail clearing happens after pointer assignment it can zero a live slot.

amanda: confirmed — i saw a memset in quant4_handoff.c right after the kvtile pointer write in one codepath. opening PR to reorder.

ben: nice find. once PR is up can we run a quick A/B: with reorder vs current on same seed to ensure divergence disappears?

amanda: yes. i'll run both and paste diffs. if the reorder fixes it i'll add a small unit that asserts no identical cache fingerprints across distinct positions.

devon: also add a canary test with rotary_scaling toggled to ensure we didn't mask an unrelated bug.

amanda: agreed. i'll coordinate with ci-bot to run the matrix (rotary on/off, int4 path on/off).

ci-bot: job ml-smoke/window-resilience/1750001234 completed: 6/6 permutations green for the reordered path, 3/6 failed on legacy path. logs: https://ci.redwood/1750001234/logs

amanda: preliminary conclusion: ordering bug in quantized tail-clear caused stale slot zeroing, hit more often with rotary_scaling due to access pattern. PR opened: https://git.redwood/pulls/4829 — includes unit and smoke.

lia: awesome. recommend adding a short e2e that streams >8k tokens in nightly to guard this class of regressions.

ben: also add a metric in console for sudden fingerprint collisions per model-version — cheap and will catch future flakiness.

amanda: noted. thanks all. :thumbsup:
